notes.text: Kailer Yamamoto is day to day (upper body injury) and missed their last game. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Michael Carcone has taken his spot beside Anders Lee and Barrett Hayton.

John Marino is on injured reserve (upper body injury) and has missed the last 6 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Andrew Peeke has taken his spot beside Nate Schmidt. That pair has had 55% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 72:38 together, about what it had with Marino (59%).

Nick Suzuki is out (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 5 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Oliver Kapanen has taken his spot beside Cole Caufield and Juraj Slafkovský. That line has had 51% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 30:10 together, down from 59% with Suzuki.
Ivan Demidov is on injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 12 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Mike Matheson is out two weeks (lower body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Lane Hutson has taken his spot beside Noah Dobson.
Oliver Kapanen is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 7 games, down from 33% last season.
Arber Xhekaj has started killing penalties: on the ice for 29% of the team’s shorthanded time in 13 games, up from 6% last season.

stakes: The Mammoth go in second in the Central with 18 points, the Canadiens second in the Atlantic with 20 points.

MTL.head: The Canadiens face a real test
MTL.body: Even though Montréal has home-ice advantage and Utah may be without Yamamoto, the Mammoth have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. On top of that, Montréal will be without Suzuki. The Canadiens’ best way through is getting good looks.

UTA.head: The Mammoth have a lot going for them
UTA.body: Even though Montréal has home-ice advantage and Utah may be without Yamamoto, the Mammoth have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. On top of that, Montréal will be without Suzuki. The Canadiens’ way back in is getting good looks.

story.head: The Canadiens are rolling
paras: The Canadiens have won five straight, and they’re rolling. The Mammoth (9-6-0) lost 6-3 to Philadelphia on Sunday. Going in, the Mammoth are second in the Central (tied for eighth in the NHL) and the Habs second in the Atlantic (fifth).

The Mammoth have played better than their record (.600) says: their chances are worth about .729, and their goaltending has held them back. The Canadiens’ record (.714) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.567), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games.

The Mammoth roll their lines more evenly than anyone (1st), rarely get pinned in their own end (1st) and let the point shots come and guard the net (2nd). As for the Canadiens, they get into more chippy games than almost anyone (2nd) and have had some of the best goaltending in the league (5th), but take more penalties than they draw (32nd). Something has to give when the Mammoth’s shooting runs into the Canadiens’ defense, and the Mammoth have the edge over the Canadiens on preventing dangerous shots.

Clayton Keller (4 G / 14 A / 18 P in 15 GP) leads the Mammoth in scoring. Logan Cooley (8 G / 9 A / 17 P in 15 GP) has a team-high eight goals, with eight points in his last five games. For the Canadiens, Lane Hutson (3 G / 10 A / 13 P in 14 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Cole Caufield (8 G / 4 A / 12 P in 14 GP) has a team-high eight goals.
Karel Vejmelka (6-5-0 / .868 SV% in 11 GS) has struggled for Utah so far, but will likely start. Jacob Fowler (7-1-0 / .932 SV% in 8 GS) has been outstanding for Montréal and will likely start.
